# Chapter One: The Dawn of Subjugation

The two men dirty and disheveled entered the small town and slowly made their way in the dead of night towards the stone building of the keep.

It had been nearly eight days since they had come ashore walking the thirty miles to this small hamlet on the outskirts of Vicor.

Nero was exhausted, his mind still reeling over the events at the small shore town, and with the death of Jorun, the old man had sacrificed himself to save the two of them, only to be massacred before there very eyes.

What was happening he wondered, what were these creatures and how was the crown involved.

These questions and more had spun around in his brain since they stepped off the boat onto dry land.

Korlin had been unusually silent for the journey citing only the creatures had indeed had magic but they were not mages, not in the sense he was.

They are twisted, perversions of magic he had said, and then had refused to speak anymore on the subject.

The two walked across the common area of the town, the first thing that Nero noticed was the lack of guards at the gate and the inn looked closed, he had never seen an inn closed this early in the evening he thought.

The large keep with its protective stone walls beckoned him, here he would find sanctuary and food he thought, a small smile of relief creeping onto his face for the first time since leaving to find the girl.

They had failed in that endeavor and it still bothered him, but something bigger was afoot and he had a duty to report to his order, the journey had opened more questions and a plot that he could not even yet begin to comprehend.

Korlin seemed to have something on it, but he would not say instead keeping the information close to his vest.

Nero thought it might concern some private Order matter, but even then the two had barely escaped alive, didn’t that entreat him to know what the other man might think on the situation he wondered, eyeing Korlin who looked no better then he, shuffling next to him, dirty and disheveled from there days of walking.

Looking himself over he could see the holes and dirt covering the heavy overcoat, Nero did his best to clean and straighten it as they approached the large wooden doors of the towns keep.

It would do no good to greet his fellow messenger looking like a vagabond he reflected, wiping some of the mud off the front of the dark wool coat.

Standing in front of the large entrance Nero took a breath calming himself before knocking on the door.

He listened carefully and soon heard the tell tale shuffling as the Messenger inside came to find out what the ruckus was. He didn’t know this keep or this messenger, but like all the houses of Aurtus he would be welcome he knew.

The door opened slightly and a harried old man looked out upon the two with suspicious eyes.

Nero thought this odd behavior from a man of Aurtus, they were trained to provide aid to all those in need he mused smiling at the older man.

“Brother, I am Messenger Nero, a long way from home, my friend and I are in need of food and shelter for a time before we continue on our journey home” he said and expected the door to open, when it didn’t he cocked his head, and looked to the old messenger.

“Brother, does thou not provide the hospitality as an emissary of this keep?” he asked. “What is the first truth of Aurtus” the raspy voice asked from the half closed door and Nero frowned

“Treat others with honor and respect that you desire for yourself” he stated knowing full well every messenger knew the truths of aurtus, it was the first thing taught to young initiates in the church.

The old man continued to eye him for a moment, then opening the door he quickly looked around before ushering the two inside.

“Quickly before anyone sees you” he whispered and Korlin and Nero hurried through the door.

“Brother, what is wrong, since when is it a crime to offer comfort in the house of Aurtus?” he asked wondering what the hell had happened here.

“Keep your voice down lest someone hear you” the old messenger hissed, Nero looked the man over now seeing his arm in a sling and the obvious limp as he motioned the two to join him, the old man limping back towards his private quarters.

The annoyed rebuke died quickly in Nero’s throat as he looked the man over, someone had beaten him and badly from the looks of it, Nero had seen enough to know that the world was changing and not for the better, so motioning to Korlin to keep quiet they followed the old Messenger to his private chambers.

As they moved towards the back of the keep he noticed the floors of keep, the ones that always stayed pristine, even when worn as the Messengers lovingly polished them weekly were scraped and gouged as if a herd of horses had come through there, the pews were all set against the wall in a haphazard way as if thrown about without care, something had happened here he thought eyeing the rest of the large meeting room.

Finally, they came to the door of the Messengers chambers and he ushered them in with his good arm, the action looking cumbersome.

As soon as they entered the old man closed the door and Nero watched as he pushed two locks, both looking brand new as he had never seen a lock on the door of a messenger’s chambers before.

The old man noticed him staring at the locks and nodded, a wry grin on his old lined face.

“I had them installed a few days past, thanks to the local smith, I know it must look odd to you brother” he said, and Nero just nodded, waiting to hear the woeful tale this man was no doubt about to reveal to them.

The old man shuffled his way over to the counter, putting the pot on and turning up the small lantern Nero could now see the bandage on his head covering some of the thinning white hair that was mussed from sleep as well as the bulky dressing he had over his leg.

“What happened to you Messenger, something has obviously gone awry here” Nero said, looking at Korlin he could see the other man remaining silent, allowing the Messenger to take the lead, but the look on his face showed the worry Nero felt, and he nodded to his friend as he continued.

“Tell me what has happened here, who has defiled this house?” Nero pressed as the man stood there making tea seemingly oblivious for the moment to his questions.

“Where do you come from brother, have you not seen the tide of change over the land, have you not experienced the Empress’s boot on your own throat, or is it different where you are from, has your village been spared the destructive wrath of the crown?” the old man asked turning an unbelieving but hopeful look to Nero and Korlin, walking over to the table he carefully poured three cups of tea, the wisps of steam playing across the man’s hand and pot as he topped the cups off.

Despite his foul mood like all messengers the task of hospitality was ingrained into them.

Nero took a cup, nodding his thanks to the old Messenger. “We have been traveling, though we have our own woes, we have not been home in almost a month, tell me what has happened brother” Nero pressed knowing whatever it was he wouldn’t want to hear it.

Something was going bad in this land and it was obvious their experience was not the only one.

Had the rot spread throughout he wondered or was it isolated, he prayed it was but though he was innocent by most’s standards, he was no fool.

Change was sweeping the territory and the crown was no longer the benevolent rule it had been.

The old man sat and with a deep sigh smiled weakly at Nero “I apologize it has been trying and I shouldn’t take out my woes on a fellow man of Aurtus, just no guidance has come from the keep and I do my best to protect my flock, but the soldiers hold no respect for Aurtus” he said and Nero could hear the fear and doubt in his words, no guidance from the keep he thought his concern deepening.

“You have not received anything from the keep since this has begun?” Nero asked, knowing what the answer would be but not able to help himself, was it possible that the Empress had taken over the Keep, taken the Lord Regent himself he wondered, his stomach growing heavy with fear.

The old messenger shook his head sadly “Not a word” he simply said but those simple words weighed heavily on both men of the cloth.

Nero nodded solemnly “Tell me what has occurred brother” he prodded and waited as the man gathered his thoughts drinking the tea as if the action calmed him. Putting down his cup he looked at Korlin “Does your friend speak or is he a mute?” the Messenger asked eyeing Korlin.

The mage smiled nodding to the messenger “I can speak but prefer to speak when I have something useful to add to a conversation” he responded then went back to drinking his tea.

The old man laughed shaking his head “It has been a trying time, I apologize if my manners are lacking friend, you are not the one who deserves my wrath” he said in the way of an apology and Korlin nodded to the man.

Turning to Nero he regarded him for a moment “the soldiers came one week hence, they moved in and secured the town, the lioness flag flying high, so we thought nothing of it, other then they were moving through on some exercise or another. That was until they started rounding up the young boys, claiming the Empress’s right to conscription. I tried to talk to them, tried to reason with them, but I was taken before the captain and beaten for all to see, to be made an example of. I was told that Aurtus was no longer who people should look to, but to the Empress as there living goddess. They took over the keep and used it to keep the boy’s prisoner until they moved them out.” He began and Nero couldn’t believe what he was hearing.

“How was this possible, if the entire territory is experiencing this how is it Lord Regent done nothing?” he whispered but fear saturated his words as the answer screamed in his mind.

The old man looked into Nero’s eyes and he could see the defeat there. “I have had no word, despite the emergency missive I have sent, I am not sure if they are not getting through or if the Empress has taken the Lord Regent and the council of Knights” he said.

Nero sat back thinking on that, the Lord Reagant was the ultimate authority in the church, from him all of the Messengers power came.

The council of knights was made up of some of the most influential lords in the land it was not possible that the Empress had moved against them.

Despite that the Lord Regent had a standing army that guarded the keep, could the Empress have declared war on the religion itself he pondered his own worry showing through and the old man nodded, seeing his own fear mirrored in Nero.

“I see what your thinking and I have already gone down that road lad, we won’t know unless we can find out ourselves.” He finished.

“I cannot leave, they are watching us, should I disappear the village will pay the price, but if you are not at your keep then you can go, find out if our messages are getting through, get word to the Lord Regent and hopefully get help. It will not be long before they begin dragging us out and killing us as an example, messenger, these are truly the dark days” he continued shaking his head.

“There is something else, the Lord Seers have been replaced, the new ones are more like priests, but they have strange symbols covering their body and they have the powers of mages” he finished and at this Korlin looked up alarmed, there was something in his eyes, some recognition maybe Nero thought.

“What do you mean?” he finally asked his gaze alarmed as the old messenger looked at him for a moment regarding him with new suspicious eyes, Nero thought he had come to the same conclusion as he.

“They have the powers of mages, but not like the mages I have known, most of those could barely move a pebble, these Seer’s can move boulders my friend, and they are the Empress’s chosen, or so they say, they are accompanied by some kind of creature that walks like a man, but the similarity ends there, they are subservient to the Seer’s, they are evil for sure, mephis’s lapdogs if you ever see one you will understand” he finished his voice hushed.

Nero could see the fear in his eyes and hear it in his words. He shot a knowing glance at Korlin, they had both seen the creatures and knew how this man felt, in fact Nero himself was shaken to his core at the mere mention of them.

“Messenger, do you have a mage in town?” he asked, and the old man looked up with a haunted look in his eyes. “We did, until the new Lord Seer slaughtered him declaring mages who did not swear fealty to the Empress enemies of the state” he finished.

Korlin got up “I need to go” he said to Nero, but the old man laid a hand on the mage’s arm. “You can’t yet, the soldiers are out on patrol, the fact that you got in here without being stopped was a miracle but know this you won’t get out again, not without help. Wait for a few hours, get some food, and then I will get you out without them seeing, they will leave the keep alone tonight so you are safe” the old man said gently locking eyes with Korlin.

The mage looked enraged and scared, Nero understood his need to report to the Order, just as he understood his own need to discover what had happened to the keep and his people. “That’s fine, we will stay and rest for a while” Nero said glaring at Korlin who eventually sat back down, though reluctantly.

They sat in silence for a while drinking tea, until finally the old man offered food and left the room to fetch something from the larder.

As soon as he was gone Nero turned to Korlin. “You know something, what is it Korlin, what has you spooked?” he asked this time Nero would not back down, he would not allow this mage to put him off based on Order secrets, too much was at stake.

Korlin seemed to sense this and sighed in defeat, looking up at Nero.

“Normally I wouldn’t say anything, but we have seen too much you and I, I expect what I will tell you will stay between the two of us, understand this will have no bearing on changing the mind of our elders, or in defeating what is happening, but it may give a significant clue as to what’s going on” he stated and Nero nodded.

“On Aurtus’s honor, this will stay between us” The Messenger said keeping his gaze leveled at Korlin.”I don’t know it all, hell I don’t even know if most of it is related, but some of what the old man said sounded familiar, I would need to talk to the archivist to know for sure” he started his eyes going distant as he tried to recall some spark of memory that had rung during the old man’s description.

“Understand, what I am about to tell you happened generations ago, it was a dark time of our order, this was during the last days of the Mage Wars, it was a desperate time in our Order, but we all have our skeletons” he said looking pointedly at Nero and the Messenger lowered his eyes, he knew about the mage purge that his order started and nearly completed, killing wholesale those who showed the gift, deciding after the Mage uprising to purge the world of those with power.

“I understand, you don’t have to remind me Korlin, that was long ago and neither of our organizations subscribe to those doctrines” he snapped, annoyed, but there was more guilt then self righteousness in that tone.

Korlin nodded rubbing his temples as he tried to chase away an oncoming migraine.

“Long ago the order experimented with those who had the gift, some of the experiments were dark, the mistakes were monstrous, and eventually put down, I don’t know a lot of specifics because once it was uncovered the order destroyed all evidence and banned the texts of that research, but in that it was said you could enhance the power by inlaying Runes directly into the skin of a mage, it was painful and dangerous but if done right, it would increase there power one hundredfold, now I never believed it any of it, the stories sounded more like a boogyman story then reality, but based on what the old man said and what we ourselves saw…” Korlin finished looking after where the old man had exited and shaking his head.

Nero blew out a breath “How would the Empress have access to anything like that?” he asked and then stopped, hadn’t they both suspected someone in the order might be working with the Empress.

“Someone in your order is a traitor Korlin” Nero put to words that which they were both thinking and the mage nodded.

“I need to get this information back, we need to find that person, because if the Empress states any mage who doesn’t serve her is the enemy” he began and left the rest unsaid.

Nero understood the order was in danger wether they knew it or not, if the Empress thought them a danger and the Order refused to swear fealty, it was possible she would complete what the church had started so long ago.

The old man returned with some smoked meat and canned vegetables and Nero and Korlin both dug in, either of them only having eaten whatever plants they had scrounged on the trip here.

Nero stayed silent but thought about what the other man had said. If the Empress was moving against the mages and the church, what was she planning, how was it she thought complete subjugation of the population was her only choice he wondered.

Everyone had heard stories, had listened to the nobles who called her “The Black Empress” but no one ever put stock in it.

The crown had always ruled the land in peace, yes there were always complaints but that was expected with any ruler, how could anyone have seen this he thought.

“What about the council of knights, surely they wouldn’t let the Empress get away with this” Nero asked hopefully but the look the old man gave him said otherwise.

He came over, putting down the rest of the food and looked up at Nero with a painful expression.

“On the first day, they brought in a group of nobles, the ones from around the area, the new Lord Seer read an edict from the Empress, all land, money and valuables would be turned over to the crown, nobility would no longer be tolerated as everyone was to work in order to further the goals of the Empress, she would be the only nobility in Vicor” he finished.

“They protested and the Lord Seer unleashed his demons upon them, the entire group was slaughtered right in front of our eyes, the next group quickly swore fealty swearing to give up all they owned for the Empress” he finished, and Nero’s heart fell.

If that was the case then the aristocracy no longer held sway in the court, there would be no more council of knights, no one to protect the religion from the Empress.

“Eat, then we will get you on your way” the old messenger said and Nero looked at him “why won’t you come with us, surely you can see that at some point they will not have a use for you and instead kill you in front of the village as an example” Nero stated.

He understood the mentality, everything he had heard from the old man would lead to this, no one was above the Empress, that was the message they were driving home, it would be inevitable that the keep and the Messengers would be an eventual target he thought but the old man smiled at him and shook his head.

“These are my people, I will not abandon them and allow the new Lord Seer to execute them for my cowardice, I will stay” he said simply and the look he gave Nero told him there was no argument that would convince him.

Nero turned his thoughts to his own village, would they suffer the wrath of the Empress now that he was not there? he wondered, but he knew going back would solve nothing, his only hope was reaching the Lord Regent, maybe there was something yet they could do, the religion spanned more then just this territory perhaps the if they could get a message to the Keeps in Dever or Lusor they would send air, surely they would not allow one regent to destroy everything they had built.

He knew every territory had a Lord Reagant, they all answered to the supreme emissary but he was far to the east and Nero doubted they had heard anything about this, it was too soon he thought, if the Lord Regent was taken prisoner here, it was likely not even there neighbors would know anything had happened, the Reagant would be forced to send missives stating everything was alright and they were backing the Empress, it would be months before the other territories would send emissary’s he knew.

Some hours later, as everyone in the village slept, a long boy entered the keep from a rear entrance known only to a few.

After some urgent whispers from the old messenger he motioned for them to follow the boy. “He knows the way out of the area that will get you by the guards and the patrols, follow him and he will get you away.

If you can reach the Lord Regent, tell him of our issues and hopefully he may have a way to save us all” the old man said and Nero could hear the hope in his words, but he did not share them, he would go to the Lord Regent but based on what he had heard, he was sure there was no help to be had.

The two followed the boy as he walked the two men past a patrol and two guard posts and out into the woods, once they had reachd far enough away from the village, he pointed north and then without a word took off towards the village again.

“I guess we go north” Kolrim said looking after the young boy. Nero nodded “We are going the same way for a few days before we will be forced to split off, me to the keep and you to the order, we should make haste” Nero said and Korlin nodded to his friend as they made their way towards hope.
